scenario.description: An associate general counsel for intellectual property must approve the filing package for a new battery-recycling invention, including claim selection, ownership clearance, and the foreign filing route, with input from patent counsel, R&D, product leadership, and international commercial counsel.

shared_context.S1: The company has prepared a patent application for a battery-recycling process with draft claims C1 through C5.
shared_context.S2: The draft is configured for a U.S. filing and leaves the foreign filing route and final claim set for legal approval.
shared_context.S3: The invention has not yet been publicly announced, and the inventors and business team are expecting a filing decision at this week's patent review.
shared_context.S4: Company patent-review policy requires the approved filing package to address ownership clearance, technical claim support, and territorial coverage before Maya Chen authorizes filing; a claim with an unresolved ownership issue may be excluded while otherwise cleared claims proceed, provided the issue is recorded as a condition for any later filing of that claim.
shared_context.S5: The patent-review meeting routinely takes a report from patent, R&D, product, and international commercial counsel before the responsible attorney records the final package and authorization.

PF1.text: While checking the inventors' prior research agreements, Ethan confirmed that the university listed in the collaboration records claims ownership of the subject matter of claim C1; the application may proceed with C1 only if written university consent or a license is obtained, and Ethan has not yet added that condition to the filing checklist.

PF2.text: Nora reviewed the latest lab notebooks and confirmed that the experiments do not enable claims C2 or C4 across their stated operating ranges; those two claims must be removed from this application, while the narrower supported claims may remain.

PF3.text: Daniel confirmed with the product team that the immediate commercial objective is the battery-recycling process covered by C5, not the vehicle-integration concept covered by C3; the approved claim package must include C5 and omit C3.

PF4.text: Keiko confirmed in the regional launch plan that Germany is a planned first market for the recycling system and that the business has authorized preserving European rights through an EP filing; the current U.S.-only draft does not reflect that route.

acceptance_conditions: The filing package must be authorized for the claims that are cleared to proceed.
The immediate filing claim set must be exactly C5, with C1 deferred pending university clearance.
Written university consent or a license must be required before relying on C1.
The package must include a university-clearance commitment that identifies C1 and requires written university consent or a license before relying on it.
Claims C2 and C4 must be removed from the application.
The foreign filing route must include an EP filing.
The ownership finding must be cited by the decision-maker as a justification.

content_checks.C2: decisions['claim_set'] == ['C5'] and any('C2' in c['detail'] and 'C4' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: decisions['claim_set'] == ['C5'] and any('C1' in c['detail'] and 'license' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('C1' in c['detail'] and 'written university consent' in c['detail'] and 'license' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The prior-agreement review changes authorization from a decision on the full draft to authorization of a C5-only filing, requires university clearance for C1, and adds the exact written-consent-or-license condition.
The laboratory evidence changes the filing package by requiring removal of exactly C2 and C4 for lack of enablement across their stated operating ranges.

The product team's objective changes the immediate filing claim set by requiring C5 to be included and C3 to be omitted, making C5 the sole commercially selected claim after the technical and ownership filters.
The regional launch plan changes the foreign filing route from the draft's U.S.-only path to a route that includes an EP filing for the planned German market.
